adjudicated.ruling: No comma before the et joining the second object of donáre, with do and with the corpus rulings at ordinarium.confiteor w028 and ordinarium.orate-fratres w021: partem áliquam et societátem is one pair.

The j-form against this edition's i-form, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md. This edition prints i because the books it edits do: the 1962 typical edition sets Iesu, Ioánnem, iube and maiestátis throughout, and so does the Mszał Rzymski of the Tyniec Benedictines (Pallottinum, Poznań 1963), which is the book a Polish reader is most likely to hold. The mid-century hand missals print j; neither spelling is a different word, and the apparatus records theirs.
House rule (ORTHOGRAPHY.md): accents ARE printed on capitals, and handmissal-eo attests the practice. Ágatha has three syllables and its stress falls on the first.
No comma before the apposition Dóminum nostrum, with handmissal-eo and with the corpus ruling at ordinarium.aufer-a-nobis w018.
